
**What changed**
National NPS fell from 36.7 to 17.6 (**-19.1 pts**) between 2 February and 26 April, compared with the eight weeks before. That is based on 2,376 survey responses. The share of detractors rose from 21.1% to 30.9%.

The fall was gradual, with one sharp drop: NPS hit -8.3 in the week of 9 March, the week of an app outage. Price and value complaints went from 10.5 to 93.5 a week (8.9x), the biggest rise of any theme. Promotions and offers complaints rose too, from 1.6 to 21.9 a week.



**Where**
- **Not one place:** NPS fell in every state except ACT. NSW fell 21.7 pts against 18.1 pts for the rest of the country. Every category fell, and the three worst stores explain only 19.9% of the drop.
- **One customer group:** Gold & Platinum members' NPS fell from 35.7 to **-12.4**. They account for 52.7% of the national fall, and 89.8% of the price complaints came from them. Silver & Bronze members fell much less, from 36.9 to 26.8.
- **Competitor prices didn't change:** the price gap to competitors stayed at about 5.9% to 5.8%. This is about how top-tier members see the value they get, not an actual price change.

**What customers said**
- "As a loyalty member I expected better prices. I found the same accessories cheaper at Big W." (Hobart) Customers at Rockhampton and North Lakes left the same comment.
- In NPS surveys, members also said "Prices have crept up again and loyalty points do not make up for it" and "Checked Amazon after buying and it was twenty dollars cheaper. Not happy as a long-time member."

**What we tested**
| Hypothesis | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| State | NSW -21.7 pts vs the rest -18.1 pts | Ruled out |
| Category | Clothing -22.4 pts vs the rest -18.1 pts | Ruled out |
| Store | The three worst stores explain 19.9% | Ruled out |
| Loyalty tier | Gold & Platinum -48.1 pts, 52.7% of the fall | **Confirmed** |
| Theme | Price and value 8.9x, 1,122 complaints | **Confirmed** |
| Price | Complaints 8.9x, competitor gap flat (5.9% to 5.8%) | **Confirmed** (perception, not a price move) |
| App | 94 of 109 complaints in the week of 9 March | **Confirmed** (one-week outage, now over) |
| Delivery | Complaints 2.8x; DC deliveries 86.8% on time, 97.1% complete | Inconclusive (only customer comments; no delivery data to check) |
| Stock | Out-of-stock mentions 1.3x baseline; 4.5% name Uppababy | Ruled out |
| Campaign | Top campaign drew 0.1% of negative comments | Ruled out |
| Supply | Uppababy supplier on-time-in-full rate 91.6% to 91.7% | Ruled out |
| Quality | Bugaboo 6.8 a week vs 7.3 | Ruled out |

**What to do** (these are recommendations; I haven't changed anything)
1. **CRM:** Review what Gold & Platinum members get, and show them clearly that it beats Big W and Amazon.
2. **Pricing:** Check member prices on lines members say are cheaper elsewhere, and consider a price match for members.
3. **Category:** Fix the promotions and offers that members say feel weak.
4. **Digital:** Do a post-incident review of the 9 March outage and set up alerts.

Confidence is **Medium**. Who fell and what they complain about are both clear. But no operational change explains it: prices against competitors stayed flat, so it comes down to how members see value. Out-of-stock mentions are starting to climb (23 in the week of 20 April), so keep an eye on that.
